title.en: GDP, per capita income and the three sectors

text.en: If every farmer, factory and shop in India counted what it made in a year and we added it all, we would get the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) - a measure of how big the economy is.

GDP is the total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country in one year.
Only final goods are counted, not intermediate goods, to avoid counting the same thing twice (double counting).
Per capita income = national income / population; it shows the average income per person.
The economy has three sectors: primary (agriculture, mining), secondary (manufacturing, construction) and tertiary or services (banking, transport, education).
As an economy develops, the share of the primary sector falls and that of the tertiary sector rises.
GDP can be measured at current prices or at constant prices; real GDP (constant prices) removes the effect of inflation.
GDP growth rate shows how fast the economy is expanding; it does not show how income is shared or the state of the environment.

problem.en: A state has a national income of Rs 4 000 crore and a population of 2 crore. Find its per capita income.

text.en: Per capita income = national income / population.

prompt.en: What is GDP and why do we count only final goods?

requiredIdeas.en: Total value of final goods and services

points.en: GDP = value of final goods and services in a year.
Per capita income = national income / population.
